**Astur v2.8.0** — one key that brings back every minimized window, and the
"next monitor" workspace keys kept on the screens you choose.

## Download

`astur-windows-x64.zip` — unzip it anywhere and run `astur.exe`. No installer, no
admin rights. The zip holds two files side by side:

- `astur.exe` — the window manager (single Rust binary)
- `astur_settings.py` — the settings editor (Python 3 with tkinter)

## What's new

### Alt+V brings everything back

`main_key` + `V` (`key_restore_all`) restores **every** minimized window of the
focused monitor's workspace, however it was minimized: the ones `main_key` + `Q`
hid, the taskbar's, an application's own. The workspace is laid out again in one
pass, floating windows come back in front of the tiles, and the focus stays where
it was — unless the focused window was one of the minimized ones, in which case
the topmost restored window takes the focus.

Restored windows also leave `Q`'s ledger, so pressing `Q` twice afterwards
restores only what `Q` itself hid and never a second copy of these. A window
hidden to the tray is not minimized, so `V` leaves it hidden.

The action is available to `extra_hotkeys` and bar clicks as `restore_all` too.

### The three workspace keys, on two screens

`switch_ws_monitors` limits where `main_key` + `L` / `;` / `'` — the 1st / 2nd /
3rd workspace of "the next monitor" — may go. `all` is the default and keeps the
old rule.

- List screen numbers, left to right starting at 1 — the same numbering as
  `monitor_layouts` and the bar's `monitors`: `switch_ws_monitors = 1 2`.
- Two or more screens listed: each press moves to the next listed screen,
  skipping the others, and wraps around. A screen that is not listed is never a
  destination, but pressing the keys there still takes you to the nearest listed
  screen.
- Exactly one screen listed: the three keys always go to that screen's 4th /
  5th / 6th workspace, from any screen.
- The setting is only read on a desktop with three or more screens. With one or
  two, the keys behave exactly as before.
- `main_key` + `,` `.` `/`, the workspace numbers, the bar pills, the wheel and
  YASB are untouched.

### Floating windows get their own border colour

`float_focused_border` and `float_unfocused_border` colour a window that is out
of the layout, so a dialog or a settings window stands apart from the tiles.
Leave them empty and floating windows keep the tiled colours — which is exactly
what existing configs get.

### A documentation site

<https://ruoyu0088.github.io/Astur/> is new: a landing page and a full manual
covering tiling, layouts, workspaces, scrolling, the bar, the launcher and system
menu, hotkeys, settings, the config files, window rules and troubleshooting, with
screenshots of each. Plain HTML and CSS: no build step, no JavaScript, no
external requests.

## Fixed

- **The README had drifted from the program.** Several defaults, key names and
  descriptions of the settings editor were out of date; it now matches the
  built-in templates and the editor.
- **Small site fixes**: the keyboard tabs switch reliably, the manual's sidebar
  no longer overlaps the content, the hero's key hint points at the right chord,
  the screenshots fit their slots, and the system-menu key is marked like the
  other shortcuts.

## Settings editor

- Covers **127** `astur.conf` keys and **74** `navbar.conf` keys, checked one by
  one against the built-in templates.
- `key_restore_all` is a key dropdown on the **Hotkeys** page, next to
  `key_minimize_window`; `switch_ws_monitors` is a text field beside the six
  workspace keys; the two floating border colours are in **Appearance**.
- `Ctrl+F` still finds every setting by name, label or help text.

## Notes

- Existing `%USERPROFILE%\.astur\astur.conf` and `navbar.conf` files are never
  rewritten. New keys reach new installs, and **Restore defaults** in the editor
  picks them up per section.
- Defaults are unchanged: Right Alt is still the main key. `V` joins the letter
  binds (`Q P V` plus `D A Z C S T F W E`), and `switch_ws_monitors = all` means
  the multi-monitor keys do what they always did until you list screens.
